beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What does a finite person owe an unchosen world?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This essay examines responsibility from childhood and ordinary decisions to institutions and divine creation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It distinguishes causing harm, answering for actions, and responding to suffering.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Examples consider poverty, work, citizenship, scientific knowledge, and automated decisions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Philosophical arguments meet research on agency, cooperation, and collective behavior.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The discussion explores obligations toward people who cannot answer for themselves.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central question concerns what a finite person owes an unchosen world.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This invitation is for readers examining agency, collective obligation, institutions, and moral luck.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Read Responsibility to follow the complete argument, examples, and consequences.
